paper_id: Qian et al. - 2021 - AIRCODE Hidden Screen-Camera Communication on an Invisible and Inaudible Dual Channel
title: AIRCODE: Hidden Screen-Camera Communication on an Invisible and Inaudible Dual Channel
motivation: Video viewers desire extra information but wireless connections require explicit setup, have latency/jitter issues, and cause information leakage.
problem_framing: Hidden screen-camera communication faces three contradicting goals: unobtrusiveness to human eyes, high data rate, and reliability.
key_insight: Use complementary advantages of dual channels: inaudible audio (~0 PER) as reliable control channel for metadata, invisible visual as high-rate data channel.
method_signature: Visual odometry screen tracking + near-ultrasound audio control channel + adaptive concatenated coding on visual data channel.
evaluation_criteria: BER, throughput/goodput, PER, screen-tracking accuracy, imperceptibility (user study), parameter sensitivity (distance, angle, signal strength, interference).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Goodput abruptly decreases when distance >90cm; larger data cells needed at longer distances. Acoustic channel may congest with multiple coexisting screens. Audio control channel requires same-room proximity.
evidence_for_taste: highly accurate screen detection is necessary
metadata is more important than data
enhancing the signal does not help
facing the dilemma of three contradicting goals
small but intolerant deviations of screen tracking
complementary advantages of video and audio
first time, enabling not only texts but also videos
